nodes.summary: The semicircle density $p(x) = \frac{\sqrt{4 - x^2}}{2\pi}$ is continuous on $\mathbb{R}$. It is positive on $(-2, 2)$ and vanishes at $\pm 2$ and outside $[-2, 2]$.
nodes.title: The semicircle density is continuous

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a Hermitian $n \times n$ complex matrix with real eigenvalues $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n$, listed with multiplicity. The empirical spectral measure of $W$ is the measure $\frac{1}{n} \sum_{j=1}^{n} \delta_{\lambda_j}$ on $\mathbb{R}$, where $\delta_\lambda$ is the Dirac measure at $\lambda$; for $n = 0$ it is the zero measure.
nodes.title: Empirical spectral measure of a Hermitian matrix

nodes.summary:
Let $
u$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb{R}$ such that $x \mapsto x^{2k}$ is $
u$-integrable for every $k$, and suppose that $\int x^k \, d
u = \int x^k \, d\sigma$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, where $\sigma$ is the semicircle distribution. Then $
u = \sigma$.
nodes.title: The semicircle distribution is determined by its moments

nodes.summary: For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the function $x \mapsto x^k$ is integrable with respect to the semicircle distribution $\sigma$, a finite measure supported in $[-2, 2]$. So the moments $\int x^k \, d\sigma$ are genuine integrals.
nodes.title: Powers are integrable against the semicircle distribution

nodes.summary: For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the semicircle distribution $\sigma$ satisfies $\int x^{2k+1} \, d\sigma(x) = 0$; in particular $\sigma$ has mean $0$. (The density is even.)
nodes.title: The odd moments of the semicircle distribution vanish

nodes.summary: For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the $2k$-th moment of the semicircle distribution $\sigma$ is the number of Dyck words of semilength $k$, the words of $k$ up-steps and $k$ down-steps none of whose prefixes has more down-steps than up-steps: These words encode the non-crossing pairings that survive in the moment method.
nodes.title: Semicircle moments count Dyck words

nodes.summary: For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the semicircle distribution $\sigma$ satisfies = \frac{1}{k + 1}\binom{2k}{k}.$$ So $\sigma$ has variance $C_1 = 1$, fourth moment $C_2 = 2$ and sixth moment $C_3 = 5$. In the moment method for Wigner's semicircle law, $C_k$ counts the non-crossing pairings that dominate $\frac{1}{n}\,\mathbb{E}\operatorname{tr}(W_n / \sqrt{n})^{2k}$, and this identity recognises the limit as $\sigma$.
nodes.title: The even moments of the semicircle distribution are the Catalan numbers

nodes.summary: For every function $g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, where $\sigma$ is the semicircle distribution. Both sides are Bochner integrals: the two integrands are integrable together, and each side is $0$ when its integrand is not integrable.
nodes.title: Integrals against the semicircle distribution

nodes.summary: The semicircle distribution in the statement of Wigner's semicircle law is, by definition, the proved-library semicircle distribution $\sigma$: both are Lebesgue measure on $[-2, 2]$ with density $\frac{\sqrt{4 - x^2}}{2\pi}$. So it is a probability measure (the Lean instance `isProbabilityMeasure_semicircleLaw`), and its moments are the Catalan numbers.
nodes.title: The two semicircle distributions agree

nodes.summary: The semicircle distribution is the measure $\sigma$ on $\mathbb{R}$ given by $\sigma(A) = \int_{A \cap [-2, 2]} \frac{\sqrt{4 - x^2}}{2\pi} \, dx$ for every measurable set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Semicircle distribution

nodes.summary: For every $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the semicircle density satisfies $p(x) = \frac{\sqrt{4 - x^2}}{2\pi} \ge 0$.
nodes.title: The semicircle density is nonnegative

nodes.summary: The semicircle density is the function $p : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, $p(x) = \frac{\sqrt{4 - x^2}}{2\pi}$, where the square root of a negative number is taken to be $0$. So $p$ is $\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{4 - x^2}$ on $[-2, 2]$ and vanishes outside it.
nodes.title: Semicircle density

nodes.summary: The semicircle distribution $\sigma$ gives no mass to the complement of $[-2, 2]$: $\sigma(\mathbb{R} \setminus [-2, 2]) = 0$.
nodes.title: The semicircle distribution is supported in [-2, 2]

nodes.summary: The Wigner semicircle distribution $\sigma$ is the measure on $\mathbb{R}$ given by $\sigma(A) = \int_{A \cap [-2, 2]} \frac{\sqrt{4 - x^2}}{2\pi} \, dx$ for every measurable set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$: Lebesgue measure on $[-2, 2]$ with the semicircle density. nodes.title: Semicircle distribution, proved library

nodes.summary: For every family of real functions $X_{ij} : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$, $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$, on a set $\Omega$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $\omega \in \Omega$, the Wigner matrix $W_n(\omega)$ is Hermitian.
nodes.title: Wigner matrices are Hermitian

nodes.summary: Let $X_{ij} : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$, for $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$, be real functions on a set $\Omega$. For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\omega \in \Omega$, the Wigner matrix $W_n(\omega)$ is the $n \times n$ complex matrix, with rows and columns indexed by $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, whose entry at $(i, j)$ is the real number $X_{\min(i, j)\, \max(i, j)}(\omega)$. nodes.title: Wigner matrix

Suppose that the family $(X_{ij})_{i \le j}$ is mutually independent, that all $X_{ij}$ with $i \le j$ have the same distribution, and that for $i \le j$ both $X_{ij}$ and $X_{ij}^2$ are integrable with $\mathbb{E}[X_{ij}] = 0$ and $\mathbb{E}[X_{ij}^2] = 1$.
